plimsoll trainer · 09 / private api lab

Private API Flight Recorder

When a model asks which warehouses are short on stock, what process calls what process? This page follows the actual messages from the model to its MCP host, through a Node gateway and a Go dataplane, into plimsoll, and back out to a private inventory API. Stockroom is a worked example, not a product. Every process boundary and every wire message below is real; only the company is invented.

The one sentence. run_javascript is the MCP tool. inventory.warehouses.list() is a runtime global inside the guest, the isolated process that runs the model-authored JavaScript. GET /v1/warehouses is a route in the Node gateway. They are three different things, and confusing them is how a private API accidentally becomes a public one.

01

Eight actors, one question

Every card is a process, an external service, or a named layer inside a process. Every line between cards is a message. Two ways to ask for the same stock data end at the same system of record and do not have the same graph.

    02

    Which of these is the MCP tool?

    MCP is the protocol the model's host uses to call an operation registered on a server. The guest global is JavaScript that exists only after plimsoll has started the isolated guest. The REST route is a private endpoint in the gateway.

    Pick one.

    03

    The bytes on each hop

    A protocol is the contract between two sides: where the bytes go, what shape they have, who answers, and what the receiver does next. Pick a hop.

    04

    Four windows into one call

    The model, the MCP wire, the guest and the private API have different contracts.

    The model sees

    • A tool named run_javascript with an input schema: code, timeoutMs.
    • A description that names the globals and points at the resource stockroom://sandbox-api.d.ts.
    • Never an origin, a token, or a route list.

    The MCP wire sends

    • JSON-RPC tools/call with the code as a string argument, over Streamable HTTP or stdio.
    • The caller's bearer to the gateway, which the gateway never forwards into the guest.
    • Back: a result with text content, and structured content when declared.

    The guest runtime gets

    • Preloaded globals: inventory.* (the preamble) over host.* (the generic client).
    • One private line to the broker; no ambient network.
    • Never the private origin, never the minted token.

    The private API receives

    • GET /v1/warehouses with a per-run JWT whose subject is the authenticated principal.
    • Only routes on the profile; a byte-for-byte match, never a decoded surprise.
    • From the broker's address, never from the guest's.

    05

    What plimsoll adds to a private API

    Stockroom keeps its domain API and its MCP product. plimsoll contributes the controlled middle: a place where agent-authored code can loop, filter and compose private data while the origin, the route policy, the caller identity, the token, the network boundary and the audit line stay outside the guest.

    Better than one-shot tools

    inventory.items.counts(id) can sit inside a loop or a condition. The model does not need one MCP round trip per item, and the advisor tells it when the loop should have been one call.

    Safer than a raw SDK secret

    The guest sees typed helpers. plimsoll holds the private origin and the per-run credential, and allows only the registered routes.

    Clearer than magic

    The MCP description and stockroom://sandbox-api.d.ts explain the model-facing contract. This page explains the process-facing one.
